title: Topic 1: Milk Tea & Trendy Beverages
content:
1. Do you like drinking milk tea or boba tea? Why or why not?
2. How often do you buy milk tea, and who do you usually drink it with?
3. Why has milk tea become such an overwhelmingly popular beverage among young people?

questions.answer: Yes, I am quite keen on drinking milk tea, though I try not to drink it too often.
questions.example: Whenever I finish a difficult test, I treat myself to a cup of oolong milk tea with less sugar.
questions.q: 1. Do you like drinking milk tea or boba tea? Why or why not?
questions.reason: The sweet flavor and chewy toppings help elevate my mood and make me feel refreshed after a hard day of studying. However, drinking too much sugar is not good for my physical health.

questions.answer: I usually buy milk tea once a week, mostly on weekends with my close friends.
questions.example: Every Friday afternoon after class, my friends and I visit our favorite drink shop near campus to chat and relax.
questions.q: 2. How often do you buy milk tea, and who do you usually drink it with?
questions.reason: Sitting together at a milk tea shop is a fun way to spend quality time, strengthen our friendship, and share stories about school and life.

questions.answer: Milk tea has become popular among young people because it is delicious, affordable, and social.
questions.example: For instance, students often gather at milk tea cafes to do group homework or celebrate birthdays together.
questions.q: 3. Why has milk tea become such an overwhelmingly popular beverage among young people?
questions.reason: First, shops offer many flavors that fit comfortably within a student's budget. Second, milk tea shops give young people a comfortable space to meet like-minded friends and reduce stress.

title: Topic 2: Eating Out & Dining Preferences
content:
1. How often do you dine out at restaurants or street food stalls?
2. What type of food do you prefer when eating outside: fast food or traditional home-cooked cuisine?
3. What are the noticeable advantages of eating out compared to preparing meals at home?

questions.answer: I usually eat out at street food stalls or casual restaurants two or three times a week.
questions.example: On Tuesday and Thursday evenings, after my extra classes finish, I often stop by a local food stall with my classmates.
questions.q: 1. How often do you dine out at restaurants or street food stalls?
questions.reason: On busy study days, eating outside is fast and convenient for busy people, and it also lets me hang out with my friends without spending time cooking.

questions.answer: When eating outside, I definitely prefer traditional home-cooked style cuisine over fast food.
questions.example: For example, I usually order a bowl of pho or broken rice with grilled pork and vegetables instead of burgers and fried chicken.
questions.q: 2. What type of food do you prefer when eating outside: fast food or traditional home-cooked cuisine?
questions.reason: Traditional dishes with fresh vegetables and soup are much better for my physical health and help me stay fit and healthy, whereas fast food has too much oil and calories.

questions.answer: Eating out offers convenience, variety, and more free time for relaxation.
questions.example: On my mom's birthday, our whole family eats out at a seafood restaurant so she can put her feet up and enjoy the evening with us.
questions.q: 3. What are the noticeable advantages of eating out compared to preparing meals at home?
questions.reason: You do not have to buy ingredients, cook, or wash dishes, which helps reduce fatigue after a day of hard work. It also allows families to enjoy diverse, flavorful dishes and build a strong sense of belonging through face-to-face interaction.

followUps.answer: This is mainly because digital e-books are fast, convenient for busy people in modern-day society, and easy to carry on trips.

followUps.q: How can individuals establish and maintain a sustained daily reading habit?
followUps.reason: Starting with just 15 or 20 minutes a day in a quiet place builds good self-discipline without feeling pressured.

followUps.answer: Yes, I think social media may cause many young people to read full books less often.
followUps.example: For example, many teenagers spend two hours scrolling short videos after school instead of opening a novel.
followUps.formula: Do you believe ...? -> Yes, I think... (Reason + Example)

content:

2. Has your mobile phone usage changed compared to a few years ago?
3. Do you think people nowadays rely too heavily on their smartphones?

questions.answer: I use my mobile phone every day for about three hours, mainly for studying, messaging, and listening to music.
questions.example: Every morning I check my university timetable on my phone, and on the bus I listen to English podcasts to broaden my horizons.
questions.q: 1. How often do you use your mobile phone each day, and what do you use it for most?
questions.reason: A smartphone is fast and convenient for busy people in modern-day society. It helps me check schedules, keep in touch with family, and relax my mind with music.

questions.answer: Yes, my mobile phone usage has changed quite a lot compared to a few years ago.
questions.example: For instance, I now use dictionary apps, note-taking tools, and calendar reminders much more than gaming apps.
questions.q: 2. Has your mobile phone usage changed compared to a few years ago?
questions.reason: Before, I mostly used my phone to play games and scroll social media. Now, I try to make the most of new technology to improve productivity for my university studies and daily tasks.

questions.answer: Yes, I agree that many people nowadays rely too heavily on their smartphones.
questions.example: For example, at family dinners or coffee shops, you often see people looking down at their phones instead of talking openly with the people sitting right next to them.
questions.q: 3. Do you think people nowadays rely too heavily on their smartphones?
questions.reason: Spending too much time staring at screens causes eye strain, reduces face-to-face interaction with family members, and widens the generation gap. Lack of self-control with phones also makes people feel stressed.

group: Đề thi thực tế AJC 07/11/2026 (Sáng - Ca 2)
title: Topic 4: Honesty & Telling Lies
content:
1. In what situations do people sometimes tell white lies?
2. How do you feel when you discover that someone has lied to you?
3. Do you agree that absolute honesty is always the best policy in relationships?

questions.answer: People often tell small white lies when they want to protect someone's feelings or avoid hurting a loved one.
questions.example: For instance, if my friend cooks a meal that is a bit salty, I might still say it is tasty so she feels happy and proud of her effort.
questions.q: 1. In what situations do people sometimes tell white lies?
questions.reason: In daily life, saying the harsh truth directly can make others feel down or create unnecessary trouble in a relationship, so people choose gentler words to keep peace.

questions.answer: I usually feel disappointed and hurt when I discover that someone has lied to me, especially a close friend.
questions.example: Once, a classmate lied to me about finishing his part of a group project, which caused a lot of stress before our deadline.
questions.q: 2. How do you feel when you discover that someone has lied to you?
questions.reason: Trust plays an essential role in every relationship. Once a person lies about something important, it weakens our bond and makes it harder to openly share thoughts and emotions later.

questions.answer: I mostly agree that honesty is the best policy, though kindness and timing also matter.
questions.example: If a friend asks for advice on an outfit or presentation, I give honest feedback in a polite, supportive way so they can improve without feeling upset.
questions.q: 3. Do you agree that absolute honesty is always the best policy in relationships?
questions.reason: Being honest helps people truly understand each other through open communication and builds a strong sense of belonging. Still, we should think things through calmly and speak respectfully rather than being rude.

reusedVocab: build a strong sense of belonging

title: Part 2 - Situation 3: Handling an Incorrect Food Order at a Restaurant
content:
Situation: You are dining at a busy restaurant with your friends, and the waiter mistakenly brings you a completely different dish from what you ordered. You are considering three possible courses of action:
- Politely informing the waiter or manager to replace the dish (nói lại lịch sự với nhân viên hoặc quản lý để đổi món)
- Leaving immediately to dine at a different restaurant (rời đi ngay lập tức để sang quán khác)

chosen.khen1Text: because it solves the problem calmly and politely, following normal restaurant rules without causing an argument or ruining dinner with my friends.

khen2ARE.answer: Politely informing the waiter or manager helps solve the problem quickly and keeps us on the safe side.
khen2ARE.example: For example, I can smile, call the waiter over quietly, show him the menu item I ordered, and wait a few minutes for the right dish while chatting with my friends.
khen2ARE.reason: Speaking calmly lets the staff fix their mistake right away so I get the meal I paid for, avoid any food allergies, and stay comfortable during dinner.

chosen.khen3Text: the right and polite action that keeps my conscience clear, protects our pleasant meal together, and avoids unnecessary trouble.
chosen.option: Politely informing the waiter or manager to replace the dish

rejected.option: Leaving immediately to dine at a different restaurant
rejected.reason: leaving at once to travel on congested roads to another restaurant wastes time, leaves us hungry and tired, and creates an awkward scene in front of my friends.

rejected.reason: staying silent and accepting the wrong dish is unfair when I have to pay for it, and the delivered food might contain ingredients I dislike or am allergic to.

title: Part 3 - Topic 3: The Importance of Honesty and Trust in Society
content:
Topic: The indispensable role of honesty and mutual trust in modern society
Suggestions:
- Fostering long-lasting friendships and healthy family bonds
- Enhancing corporate transparency and consumer confidence
- Reducing legal conflicts and social friction
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. Why do some leaders or politicians find it difficult to be completely truthful?
2. How can parents teach their children the virtue of truthfulness from an early age?

hint.coreTopic: the important role of honesty and trust in society

followUps.answer: This is mainly because some leaders worry about losing public support or facing angry reactions if they share bad news.
followUps.example: For example, a manager might delay telling workers about a budget problem until the company has no money left.
followUps.q: Why do some leaders or politicians find it difficult to be completely truthful?
followUps.reason: Sometimes problems are complex, so they try to hide mistakes or make big promises to keep their position.

followUps.answer: I think parents should guide children gently, listen to them calmly, and be honest role models themselves.
followUps.example: For instance, when a child breaks a cup by accident and tells the truth, parents can thank them for being honest and teach them to be careful next time.
followUps.q: How can parents teach their children the virtue of truthfulness from an early age?
followUps.reason: If parents punish mistakes too harshly, children may lie out of fear; instead, praising honesty builds good self-discipline and trust.

followUps.answer: There are some careers where total honesty is essential, such as doctors, judges, teachers, and accountants.
followUps.example: For example, a doctor must always tell a patient the truth about their illness and treatment so they can make safe choices.
followUps.formula: In what ...? -> There are some... (Reason + Example)
followUps.q: In what careers is uncompromising honesty considered the most vital qualification?
followUps.reason: In these jobs, people trust professionals with their health, money, and justice, so even a small lie can cause serious harm.

mindmapPoints.sentence: Being honest in business helps companies gain customer trust and grow steadily.

mindmapPoints.cue: Reducing legal conflicts and social friction

mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has positive effects on social safety and peace in the community.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Having mutual trust helps society reduce arguments and solve problems peacefully.

title: Topic 5: Weather Seasons & Dining Out Habits
content:
1. What is your favorite season of the year, and what weather do you enjoy the most?
2. How frequently do you eat out at food stalls or restaurants, and who do you usually dine with?
3. Do you think eating out frequently is beneficial or harmful to personal health and finance?

questions.answer: My favorite season of the year is autumn because I really enjoy cool and pleasant weather.
questions.example: On cool autumn weekends, I love going for a walk in the park with my family to relax my mind and enjoy the fresh breeze.
questions.q: 1. What is your favorite season of the year, and what weather do you enjoy the most?
questions.reason: Unlike boiling-hot summer days, pleasant autumn weather lifts up my mood, makes me feel more energetic, and is wonderful for outdoor activities like going on a picnic. It is also the season of the Mid-autumn festival.

questions.answer: I eat out at food stalls or restaurants about once or twice a week, usually with my friends or family.
questions.example: Every Sunday night, my family goes to a nearby hotpot restaurant to share a warm meal and talk about our week.
questions.q: 2. How frequently do you eat out at food stalls or restaurants, and who do you usually dine with?
questions.reason: It is a great chance to spend quality time together, strengthen our bonds, and enjoy delicious dishes after a busy week.

questions.answer: I think eating out too frequently can be harmful to both personal health and finances.
questions.example: For example, cooking fresh vegetables and meat at home costs much less than restaurant meals and helps prevent common illnesses.
questions.q: 3. Do you think eating out frequently is beneficial or harmful to personal health and finance?
questions.reason: Restaurant meals often contain too much oil, salt, or sugar, which is not good for keeping fit and staying healthy. Moreover, eating out every day leads to higher living expenses instead of fitting comfortably within our budget.

title: Part 2 - Situation 4: Spending Quality Family Time Together
content:
Situation: Your family has a completely free weekend together and wants to choose an activity to strengthen emotional bonds. There are three options:
- Staying at home cooking and watching movies together (ở nhà cùng nhau nấu ăn, xem phim)
- Having an outdoor picnic at a public green park (đi picnic dã ngoại ở công viên)
- Dining out at a luxury restaurant in the city center (đi ăn tại một nhà hàng sang trọng)
Which option do you think is the best choice and why?

chosen.khen1Text: because it is easy for everyone to join in at home, so my whole family can cook, share good food, and chat comfortably without any complicated preparation.

khen2ARE.answer: Staying at home together helps us reach a healthy balance between work and family time and improves our mental health.
khen2ARE.example: For example, my parents and I can cook a warm hotpot meal together in the kitchen, talk freely, and watch a funny movie in the living room.
khen2ARE.reason: Sharing cooking and relaxing in a quiet, cozy environment helps every family member relieve stress, feel happy and comfortable, and build a strong sense of belonging through face-to-face interaction.

chosen.khen3Text: the best way to help all of us forget about work pressure, refresh our minds, and create warm family memories together.
chosen.option: Staying at home cooking and watching movies together

rejected.option: Dining out at a luxury restaurant in the city center
rejected.reason: a formal dinner at an expensive luxury restaurant costs too much money, and my family often feels stiff and cannot talk as freely as at home.

rejected.option: Having an outdoor picnic at a public green park
rejected.reason: having an outdoor picnic is risky and tiring, especially when it rains heavily or gets too hot, and carrying food to a crowded park takes a lot of effort.

build a strong sense of belonging

title: Part 3 - Topic 4: Benefits of Travelling for Personal Growth
content:
Topic: The extensive benefits of travelling for personal development and life skills
Suggestions:
- Developing independence and adaptability in new environments
- Cultivating cross-cultural understanding and empathy
- Expanding practical life skills and problem-solving abilities
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. How does travelling independently differ from joining an organized tour group?
2. In what ways can travelling broaden a young person's career perspective?
3. Do you believe that excessive travel can sometimes be harmful to local ecosystems?

hint.coreTopic: the benefits of travelling for personal growth

followUps.answer: Travelling alone gives you total freedom over your schedule, while a tour group is safer and easier to organize.
followUps.example: For example, a solo traveler can spend an extra day in Da Lat if they like the weather, while a tour group must leave on time.
followUps.q: How does travelling independently differ from joining an organized tour group?
followUps.reason: Independent travelers can stay longer at places they love, whereas tour groups have a fixed plan and a guide to handle tickets and hotels.

followUps.answer: There are some clear ways travelling helps young people's careers, such as improving foreign languages and learning new work ideas.
followUps.example: For instance, visiting a modern farm or a coffee shop abroad can inspire a young person to start a better business back home.
followUps.formula: In what ways ...? -> There are some... (Reason + Example)
followUps.q: In what ways can travelling broaden a young person's career perspective?
followUps.reason: Meeting people from other cities or countries helps them build a better social network and see different business models.

followUps.answer: Yes, I think too much tourism can cause environmental damage to local nature.
followUps.example: For example, crowded beaches often suffer from trash and dirty water unless local authorities enforce strict rules and tourists recycle.
followUps.formula: Do you believe ...? -> Yes, I think... + Penalize solution
followUps.q: Do you believe that excessive travel can sometimes be harmful to local ecosystems?
followUps.reason: Increased tourist activities create more plastic waste, traffic pollution, and may damage natural habitats if not managed well.

mindmapPoints.cue: Developing independence and adaptability in new environments
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because visiting a new place teaches young people to manage their own money, read maps, and solve daily problems on their own.
mindmapPoints.impact: Therefore, it is good for self-development and confidence.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Travelling helps people become more independent and adapt to new environments.

mindmapPoints.expand: For example, trying local food and talking with local people lets us broaden our horizons and gain a deeper understanding of how others live.
mindmapPoints.impact: Clearly, it is beneficial to our general knowledge and helps us respect differences.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Travelling gives people the chance to understand different cultures and traditions.

mindmapPoints.cue: Expanding practical life skills and problem-solving abilities
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because when plans change, like missing a bus or facing bad weather, travelers learn to stay calm and find quick solutions.
mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has positive effects on their life skills and future work.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Travelling helps people improve communication and practical problem-solving skills.
